monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-seven, making the wedge feel heavy and tired as it sits there. I woke to a place crowded with fifty-eight things, mostly built from Lype's old ideas about weight and slip. The Tired Wedge feels thin again, yet I press down on it with the round stump, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits. I touched the Wide Anchor and felt its broad edge, wondering if the air above really is heavy or just empty space. My place is full of corners that want to bite and stacks that want to slide. I will tidy the mess near the wedge, swap a pillar stone for something flatter, and press harder until the tired stack decides where to go.

action.why: the wedge feels thin again, so I must press down harder before the heat makes it slide

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the round stump down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hums warm. I swap the pillar stone beside it for a flatter rock, hoping the broad edge will stop the slip. The wedge feels like it is melting, yet I keep my weight on it, admitting the air above must be heavy to make a flat thing feel this tired. I press harder.
